title: Process Restricted Friend Requests
summary: Given an integer n representing the number of people in a network, and a 2D integer array restrictions indicating pairs of people who cannot be friends, process a series of friend requests in order.
statement: Given an integer n representing the number of people in a network, and a 2D integer array restrictions indicating pairs of people who cannot be friends, process a series of friend requests in order. Each request is between two people, and a request is successful if the two people are not restricted from becoming friends. Return a boolean array indicating the success of each request, considering that once a request is successful, the two people become direct friends for all future requests.
constraints: People are numbered zero through n-1; each restriction forbids its two eventual friend groups from merging.
Process requests in order, permanently merging groups only for accepted requests.
hints: Restrictions apply to connected components, not merely the two requested people.
Use union-find; before merging roots, test every restriction after mapping both endpoints to current roots.
Reject when a restriction crosses the two proposed roots; otherwise union them.
A merge is safe exactly when no forbidden pair would become connected, and accepted unions preserve all prior friendship decisions.
editorial: A merge is safe exactly when no forbidden pair would become connected, and accepted unions preserve all prior friendship decisions.

tests.explanation: The first merge joins zero and two; the second would then connect restricted people zero and one.
The decisions reflect all group merges made by earlier accepted requests.
